newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH PRIMARY T-BILL DEALERS UP TO 59 IN Q4 1996.
newsitem.headline: POLISH PRIMARY T-BILL DEALERS UP TO 59 IN Q4 1996.

text.p: The number of Polish primary T-bill dealers rose in the fourth quarter of 1996 to 59 from 55 in the third quarter, the National Bank of Poland said in a statement on Tuesday.
The status of a primary T-bill dealer entitles banks and non-banking institutions to buy Polish treasury bills directly at the finance ministry's regular primary tenders each Monday.
The group of banks with the privilage increased by Polish branches of BNP-Dresdner Bank SA, Westdeutsche Landesbank SA, and Bank Komunalny SA in Gdynia.
One domestic bank, Bank Pocztowy SA in Bydgoszcz, lost the status bringing the total number of banks in the fourth quarter to 48 against 46 in third quarter.
Two newcomers from the domestic non-banking sector -- the Turow power plant and Poland's biggest refinery Petrochemia Plock -- brought their total number to 11 from nine in third quarter.

The retain the status of a primary T-bill dealer next year participants will have to buy 18.5 million zlotys in nominal terms worth of T-bills during the fourth quarter, down from 22.68 million zlotys in the third quarter.
